texts.preamble: Ashish Gupta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 December, 2024 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:190569 Court No. - 80 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 2085 of 2008 Revisionist :- Ashish Gupta Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :- Apul Misra Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. Heard Sri Apul Misra, learned counsel for the revisionist, Sri Ajay Singh, learned Aga-I for the State and perused the records. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.6, Jhansi in Complaint Case No.1443 of 2000 (R.P. Srivastava, Food Inspector, Bada Gaoin, Jhansi Vs. Ashish Gupta) convicting the revisionist of charges under Section 16 (1)(a)(ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced him Ashish Gupta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106738339/ 1 for six months R.I. and fine of Rs.1,000/- and in default of payment of fine further to undergo one month S.I. 3.
texts.arguments: At the outset, learned counsel for the revisionist does not challenge his conviction, but submits that he is ready and willing to apply for commutation of sentence on the condition of further deposit, if any, in lieu of awarded sentence. 4. Learned A.G.A. submits that the sentence is proportionate to the charge established. He also submits that no useful purpose would be served by keeping this revision pending and it be disposed of by giving appropriate directions. 5. It is not disputed that the alleged offence took place on 5.11.1997, when the alleged sample of turmeric purchased from the revisionist was found to be adulterated. However, the Court cannot be oblivious that an offence under the P.F.A. Act has serious ramifications in the society, which cannot be lightly ignored, but at the same time to direct him after 17 years to serve out his remainder sentence is the other extreme. Learned A.G.A. is right in his submission that this Court cannot tinker, where minimum sentence is provided under a statute like the P.F.A. Act, 1954. 6. The Apex Court in the case of State of Rajasthan Vs. Jagdish Prasad : (2009) 12 SCC 646 held in paras-4 and 5 thereof as under: "4. In Dayal Singh v. State of Rajasthan it was inter alia observed as follows: (SCC pp. 728-29, para 15) "15. In the instant case it was not disputed that for the offence charged a minimum sentence of 6 months' rigorous imprisonment is prescribed by law. We are not inclined to modify the sentence by passing an order of the nature passed in N. Sukumaran Nair where this Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction imposed only a sentence of fine and directed that State to exercise its powers under Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine. If no order in the matter of commutation is passed by the appropriate Ashish Gupta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106738339/ 2 Government the accused shall surrender to custody to serve the remainder of sentence." Learned counsel for the revisionist has also expressed his willingness that the revisionist is prepared to apply for commutation of sentence under Section 433 of the Code and is also willing to deposit additional fine.
